messages:
david.platform: Heads-up — I'm drafting the Private deploy KMS integration playbook. Quick q: For control-plane secrets + dataplane DEKs, are we leaning envelope encryption with a single CMK per-customer or a cross-account key per-region? Need plan for rewrap on rotation and how the proxy should cache DEKs.

alice.sec: I recommend 1 CMK per-customer per-region (alias/customer-<id>-cmk). Use GenerateDataKey to return plaintext DEK to the control-plane proxy, encrypt DEK using CMK (CiphertextBlob) and store the encrypted DEK with resource metadata. Proxy caches plaintext DEK in memory with strict TTL (e.g., 5m) + KMS grants for the proxy role. Use encryption context to bind: {"purpose":"redwood:dataplane-dek","customer":"<cust-id>"}.

ben.sre: Notes: avoid long-lived plaintext caches. If we need faster tokenization we can use local AES key cached in RAM, rotate quickly. For rotation: enable automatic CMK rotation, then run rewrap job that does Decrypt(CiphertextBlob) -> GenerateDataKeyWithoutPlaintext? Hmm better: Decrypt -> Encrypt with new CMK -> store. Example CLI:
```
# rewrap existing encrypted DEK
PLAINTEXT=$(aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://encrypted_dek.bin --encryption-context Purpose=redwood:dataplane-dek --query Plaintext --output text | base64 --decode)
aws kms encrypt --key-id alias/customer-1234-cmk --plaintext fileb://- --encryption-context Purpose=redwood:dataplane-dek > rewrapped.enc
```

carla.sre: Small corrections: use --query Plaintext returns base64, decode then pass to encrypt. Also prefer using GenerateDataKey to avoid handing plaintext across the wire when provisioning new DEKs. For rotation of many DEKs we should run a streaming rewrap job that decrypts with old key (via KMS Decrypt) and re-encrypts with new key, respecting encryption context and using a temporary ephemeral worker role with kms:ReEncrypt rights. Use KMS ReEncrypt API which does it server-side:
```
aws kms re-encrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://encrypted_dek.bin --destination-key-id alias/customer-1234-cmk --source-encryption-context Purpose=redwood:dataplane-dek --destination-encryption-context Purpose=redwood:dataplane-dek
```
This avoids plaintext handling.

david.platform: Good — ReEncrypt is ideal.

alice.sec: Also: grants vs IAM: grant for passing plaintext is safer and auditable; use GrantTokens for short lived. Endpoint restrictions: create VPC Endpoint for KMS (com.amazonaws.<region>.kms) and apply endpoint policy limited to that CMK. Alternatively, use KMS key policy that limits principals to the redwood-controlplane role and the service account.

ben.sre: For dataplane nodes (in-customer VPC) they will need access to rewrap when we rotate? Plan: control plane does rewrap and pushes newly encrypted DEK to dataplane agents via secure channel (mTLS). Dataplane should only have ability to decrypt DEK using KMS if they have appropriate role (edge-case for private on-prem: customers will supply BYOK or we host a proxy to handle DEKs).

carla.sre: Action items:
- create CMK alias and key policy template (alice)
- endpoint + endpoint policy (ben)
- rewrap automation using kms:ReEncrypt (carla)
- add encryption-context enforcements in code and telemetry (david)

alice.sec: quick policy snippet:
```
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {"Effect":"Allow","Principal":{"AWS":"arn:aws:iam::111222333444:role/redwood-controlplane"},"Action":["kms:Encrypt","kms:Decrypt","kms:ReEncrypt*","kms:GenerateDataKey"],"Resource":"*","Condition":{"StringEquals":{"kms:EncryptionContext:Purpose":"redwood:dataplane-dek"}}}
  ]
}
```

david.platform: thx. let's try to keep the next deploy to draft the playbook and schedule a run in staging. FYI flagged for compliance: we need audit logs + CloudTrail events for Decrypt/ReEncrypt. @compliance please review.

kms-bot: New audit rule created: monitor KMS ReEncrypt and Decrypt events for customer-* CMKs. :white_check_mark:

ben.sre: :thumbsup: I'll create a staging runbook and a one-off lambda to test rewrap on a small sample.

carla.sre: I'll set up a canary that rewraps a single DEK and verifies the dataplane accepts it.

david.platform: cool. tagging this thread for the playbook. anyone opposed to 5m caching and 7d rotation window? speak up now.

alice.sec: 5m cache is fine for control plane. rotation every 90 days preferred; 7d window is OK for phased rollout.

ben.sre: agree.

carla.sre: agree.

david.platform: closing — will open playbook PR with details.
